stem: In a common dry cell, electrolyte is –
expl: In a common dry cell, ammonium chloride or zinc chloride is used as the electrolyte, and manganese dioxide is used as the cathode material.

stem: A photoelectric cell is a device which

options.label: a
options.text: converts light energy into electric energy

options.label: b
options.text: converts electric energy into light energy

expl: A photoelectric cell is an electronic device that converts light energy into electrical energy. It is also called an Electric Eye or a Phototube. Note that a photoelectric cell works on the principle of the photoelectric effect. A photoelectric cell consists of an evacuated glass tube in which two elec-trodes are fitted—an emitter and a collector.

stem: Solar cell is a device that converts light energy into electrical energy. We obtain the highest output of energy during noon when the sun is just above our head, because :

options.label: b

expl: At noon, the Sun’s rays fall vertically on the solar collector; therefore, the density of the incident light radiation received is maximum. Hence, solar energy production is maximum at noon.

stem: The magnetic needle points to –
expl: A magnetic needle points towards the north direction. It aligns itself according to the Earth’s magnetic poles (north and south). Therefore, the needle is attracted towards the Earth’s north magnetic pole and indicates the north direction.

stem: The paramagnetic theory of magnetism applies to –

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Paramagnetism is a form of magnetism in which some materials are weakly attracted by an externally applied magnetic field and produce an induced magnetic field in the same direction as the applied field. Platinum is a paramagnetic substance.

stem: Bulbs used in street lighting are connected in-

options.label: a
options.text: Both in series and parallel order

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: All bulbs used in street lighting are connected in parallel. This is done because if bulbs are connected in series, their brightness decreases. Therefore, to obtain higher brightness, each bulb is connected in parallel.

stem: What is the device to protect equipment from the electric shock?
expl: A fuse is a safety device connected in series in an electric circuit. It is made of a thin wire or a metal strip with limited current-carrying capacity. When excessive current flows due to overload or short-circuit, the fuse wire heats up and melts, breaking the circuit. Thus, current flow stops and electrical appliances are protected from damage due to excess current.

stem: The wire generally used for installation of safety fuse is made of which material?

options.label: d
options.text: An alloy of tin and lead

expl: A fuse is a small piece of wire. It is made of a tin–lead (Sn– Pb) alloy. It has a low melting point and high resistance. Due to short-circuiting, overloading, voltage surge, etc., when the current in the circuit exceeds the specified limit, the fuse melts and breaks. This prevents damage to electrical/ electronic equipment and helps avoid possible accidents.

stem: An electric fuse works on the :

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: An electric fuse works on the heating effect of electric current. When current passes through a resistor or an appliance, resistance is encountered and heat is produced in the process; this is called the heating (thermal) effect. A fuse is a safety device that protects electric circuits and components from possible damage.

stem: Due to temperature variation along a conductor, potential variation occurs along it. This phenomenon is known as :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: When the two ends of a conductor are kept at different temperatures and an electric current flows through it, heat is evolved or absorbed along the length of the conductor; this is known as the Thomson effect.

stem: What does the speed of the fan depend on?
expl: The speed of a fan can be controlled by voltage. Voltage control is the most popular method for speed control of induction-motor-driven fans such as table fans. Fan speed can also be controlled by resistance/rheostat control, capacitor control, and power-electronic regulators (triac regulators).

stem: The material commonly used to make the core of an electromagnet is :

options.label: d

expl: The core of an electromagnet is made of soft iron (a magnetic material). Electromagnets are used in making electric bells, loudspeakers, and telegraph devices.

stem: High voltage grids are used to transmit electricity because-
expl: Electric transmission: high-voltage grids are used to increase efficiency and reduce heat loss. According to Ohm's law, a lower current results in lower resistive loss. For a fixed power (P = VI), keeping current low requires a high value of voltage.

expl: A bar magnet Placed in the Earth's magnetic field with its North Pole pointing towards geographic North, has 2 neutral points around it.

stem: Which of the following metals is used as filament in lighting bulbs?
expl: Generally, the resistivity of alloys is higher than that of the pure metals from which they are made. Also, the rate of change of resistivity with change in temperature is comparatively low. Therefore, they do not oxidize quickly at high temperatures. For this reason, they are used in common electrical heating devices like electric presses, toasters, etc. For making filaments of incandescent lamps, only tungsten is used, whereas copper and aluminium are used to make wires for electric transmission.

stem: Semiconductors are materials that have the following properties -

expl: Semiconductors are substances whose electrical conductivity is less than that of conductors, but greater than that of insulators. For example, silicon (Si) and germanium (Ge) are semiconductors.

stem: Which one of the following metals is used as a semiconductor in transistors?
expl: The electrical resistance of some materials like silicon and germanium lies between that of conductors and insulators; such materials are called semiconductors. They generally conduct electricity, but when small amounts of impurities are added, their conductivity increases and they become n-type and p-type semiconductors, which are used in transistors.

options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Semiconductors are solid substances whose resistivity is greater than that of conductors but less than that of insulators. The resistance of a semiconductor decreases when temperature increases.

stem: The characteristic of a superconductor is –
expl: In 1911, the Dutch physicist H. K. Onnes (1853–1926) studied the effect of temperature on resistance. He cooled some metal samples to a few kelvins and measured their electrical resistance. He found that at a very low temperature (around 4.2 K), the electrical resistance of mercury becomes zero. Later, it was found that many elements and compounds behave similarly at low temperatures. Such substances are called superconductors. Since superconductors show no resistance, there is no loss of energy when current flows through them. Therefore, superconductors can be used efficiently for transmitting electricity from one place to another. Another essential property of superconductors is that they prevent magnetic flux from entering their interior The magnetic field/flux is confined to the surface, i.e., their magnetic permeability is zero.

stem: Lenz’s law is derived from the law of conservation of

expl: Lenz’s law is based on the law of conservation of energy. It ensures that in the process of electromagnetic induction, energy is neither created nor destroyed. The induced current always opposes the change due to which it is produced. Hence, Lenz’s law is based on energy conservation.

stem: The process of charging a conductor by bringing it near another charged conductor, without making any contact, is called–

expl: The process of charging a conductor by bringing it near another charged conductor without making contact is defined as induction.

stem: Which of the following liquids is a bad conductor of electricity?
expl: Lemon juice, salted water, and orange juice contain dissolved ions, due to which these solutions show conductivity. All of these are conductors of electricity. Therefore, among the given options, (d) is the correct answer.

stem: The conductivity of a strong electrolyte
expl: A strong electrolyte has high conductivity. Strong electrolytes ionize completely in water. When a strong electrolyte is diluted, the number of ions per unit volume decreases; therefore, its conductivity decreases. Examples of strong electrolytes are NaCl, KCl, etc.
